newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi clarifies welfare reform comments.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi clarifies welfare reform comments.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi on Wednesday clarified recent comments that some had interpreted as suggesting the government wanted to get pensions reforms started next month.
"I did not say that the government wanted to carry out reforms in May," Ciampi told a news conference.

According to a parliamentary summary released on Tuesday, Ciampi told a budget committee that the government's annual document of three-year rolling economic targets (DPEF) would set out "strategic lines" for pension reforms.
The DPEF is due to be presented in May.
Ciampi said on Wednesday that "when the government presents the DPEF more or less in the middle of May it needs to indicate how to proceed on certain points.
"It will be more or less explicit depending on how the developments on this subject unfold," he said, adding that it would not contain precise figures.

Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco, at the same news conference, said the DPEF would contain a macro economic framework for the Italian economy for the next few years as well as points relating to budget policy.

The centre-left government of Prime Minister Romano Prodi has placed welfare reform high on the agenda as it fights to straighten out public finances and win a place in Europe's planned currency union from the outset.
However it faces opposition from trade unions and its hard-left parliamentary allies Communist Refoundation to make any changes before 1998.

Prodi has said welfare reforms would be included in the 1998 budget to be approved by the end of the year after consultation with all components of the centre-left majority, employers and trade union representatives.

Ciampi's remarks on Tuesday drew fire from unions and Refoundation who saw it as an attempt to force the agenda. Bertinotti said after Ciampi's comments on Tuesday: "If (reform) starts like this, it will never start".
Centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi also criticised Ciampi, saying that he had little confidence in any DPEFs presented by the government.

However the president of the business federation Confindustria Giorgio Fossa welcomed Ciampi's stated intention to insert indications about reforms into the DPEF, while warning that rifts were again evident in the centre-left.

"Ciampi's position will be considered positively, but there are already statements, once again from a part of the majority and the unions, that do not seem to me to share Ciampi's intentions," Fossa told reporters.

"We must see when the talks effectively start and whether they manage to get the results that I hope for and which are those stated yesterday by Minister Ciampi," he said. -- Rome newsroom 39 6 678 2501
